description: The Newcastle Urban Observatory, run by Newcastle University and listed as a UKCRIC facility, describes itself as the largest set of publicly available real-time urban data in the UK. All data are published as open data, available through an API or by download: users choose a location and variables, live data refresh second by second, and historical archives can be downloaded across many sectors. The version 2 sensor API listed 1,539 entities on 26 September 2026, each with feeds and time series such as nitric oxide from national air quality (AURN) stations, with links to raw and historic series. Coverage: Newcastle upon Tyne; the API sample read here showed air quality feeds from national monitoring stations. Access: open API and downloads; the portal is a JavaScript application. Licence: open data, name not stated on the pages read. Caveats: some feeds come from third-party networks and brokers, some marked inactive, and sensor coverage changes over time. Simulation uses: live and historical urban sensing to drive and validate city digital twins, heat and air quality models. Related records: the Array of Things in Chicago.
